title: st.audio_input in the sidebar shows "An error has occurred, please try again." after a successful recording
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `st.audio_input` is rendered inside `st.sidebar`, stopping a recording shows "An error has occurred, please try again." in place of the waveform. The upload itself succeeds: the script receives the file, and `st.audio` can play it back. The same code in the main area works correctly.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

with st.sidebar:
    audio = st.audio_input("Record", key="voice_audio")
    if audio is not None:
        st.success("Audio received successfully!")
        st.audio(audio)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. In the sidebar, click **Record**, speak for a second or two, and click **Stop recording**.

### Expected Behavior

The widget shows the recorded waveform and the play/download controls, the same as in the main area.

### Current Behavior

The widget shows "An error has occurred, please try again." Meanwhile "Audio received successfully!" and the `st.audio` player render below it, and the upload `PUT /_stcore/upload_file/...` returns 204.

No console error is printed because the exception is swallowed. Logging the `catch` in the playback-load effect of `AudioInput.tsx` shows:

```
Error: Player not initialized
    at load (useWaveformController.ts)
```

**Cause.** `ThemedSidebar` calls `createSidebarTheme(activeTheme)` on every render, and that returns a new object each time:

```tsx
// frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/ThemedSidebar.tsx
const sidebarTheme = createSidebarTheme(activeTheme)
```

1. `useWaveformController`'s `initializeWaveSurfer` callback depends on `theme`.
2. A new theme identity therefore re-runs the mount effect. Its cleanup calls `destroy()`, and the effect re-initializes WaveSurfer asynchronously.
3. Stopping a recording triggers a rerun that re-renders the sidebar several times in quick succession.
4. I instrumented the DOM and saw WaveSurfer destroyed and re-created 5+ times within about 100 ms. In the main area it is created exactly once.
5. When the playback-load effect calls `playback.load()` during one of those windows, it throws `Player not initialized`, and the widget enters its error state.

Wrapping the call in `useMemo(() => createSidebarTheme(activeTheme), [activeTheme])` removes the churn and the error.

Local results (headless Chromium with a fake microphone, sidebar app above):

| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1.51.0 | No error (2/2). WaveSurfer is still re-created on rerun |
| 1.63.0 | Error 3/3 |
| 1.64.0 | Error 3/3 |
| 1.65.0 | Error 1/3; the other 2 runs failed at Record with `Record backend not initialized` |
| 1.66.0 | Error 1/10 |
| `develop` @ 4365bdc4 | Error 7/10; WaveSurfer torn down in 10/10 runs |
| `develop` + memoized sidebar theme | Error 0/10; no teardown |

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0 (also reproduced on 1.64.0, 1.65.0, 1.66.0, and `develop` @ 4365bdc4)
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Windows 11, Linux; also reported on mobile devices
- Browser: Microsoft Edge, Chromium

### Additional Information

The last version I tested without a visible error is 1.51.0. I did not bisect 1.52–1.62.

The churn affects any sidebar descendant that uses the Emotion theme as a hook dependency, not only `st.audio_input`. Separately, because `useWaveformController` has `theme` in `initializeWaveSurfer`'s dependencies, any legitimate theme change (light/dark switch, auto theme, host theme message) also destroys and re-creates WaveSurfer, in the main area too and for audio-enabled `st.chat_input`.

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17585)

This is a frontend regression in `st.audio_input` when it is rendered in `st.sidebar`. After the user stops recording, the upload succeeds — the script receives the file, `st.audio` can play it, and `PUT /_stcore/upload_file` returns 204 — while the widget shows "An error has occurred, please try again." The same widget in the main area shows the waveform. The current code matches that split: `ThemedSidebar` calls `createSidebarTheme(activeTheme)` on every render, so the sidebar Emotion theme is a new object each time, and `useWaveformController` lists that whole `theme` object as a dependency of `initializeWaveSurfer`. Each new theme identity re-runs the mount effect, which calls `destroy()` and creates WaveSurfer again. The rerun after stop re-renders the sidebar several times while `AudioInput`'s playback effect calls `playback.load()`; if `playerRef` is empty in that window, `load` throws `Player not initialized`, and the catch in `AudioInput.tsx` sets the error state without logging. Memoizing the sidebar theme on `activeTheme` stops those extra teardowns. Initialization should also stay tied to sample rate and the colors passed into WaveSurfer, since color updates already go through `setOptions`; a real theme change still rebuilds the player in the main area and in audio-enabled `st.chat_input`. The reporter last saw a clean waveform on 1.51.0 and reproduced the error on 1.63.0–1.66.0 and current `develop` (intermittent on some of those versions).

### Related Issues

No open duplicate turned up. Two closed issues share the waveform or the same error string, with different triggers:

- [#17528](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17528) — `st.chat_input(accept_audio=True)` kept capturing audio while the live waveform stayed empty after the text area grew past one line. That was the chat input unmounting the waveform node; it was fixed in #17579. Both widgets share `useWaveformController`, and this report also notes that a real theme change still tears that player down.
- [#9717](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9717) — the same "An error has occurred, please try again." text after stopping a ~1 hour `st.experimental_audio_input` recording. That report is about a very long take (session or buffer limits), and it is closed.
